title: Harbour
notes: Introduce the honours prototype. The question is whether local models plus explicit source checks can support everyday health-record tasks on a phone.

title: Interfaces
notes: Simple mode is the default for an independent older adult. A caregiver can expose records and review tools in Settings. Both modes use the same local account and records; this is not remote caregiver access.

title: Request processing
notes: The local LLM chooses the tool. The app validates the request against original input, resolves names from saved records and the database, and uses existing editors. It does not let generated text directly overwrite medications. Unknown interaction pairs remain unassessed; the medication-name vocabulary is not a comprehensive interaction dataset.

title: App walkthrough
callouts: Values come from records, not generated prose
notes: Play the genuine native video, or choose Live and operate the QA simulator. Pause and select Explain to lift the actual rendered table out of the phone. The recording uses Alex. Saved records are fictional; the chat tool call is actual local inference.

title: Medication names
callouts: A similar-sounding name remains a candidate
notes: The extract includes 8299 generic and unambiguous brand entries, around 1.46 MB on disk. Salt-qualified ingredients are retained. Apple recognition hints prioritize saved names and a short common-name list, capped at 100 phrases. Acoustic improvement has not yet been measured.

title: Visit review
notes: Use the saved authored fixture to demonstrate the review UI, not to imply this example was correctly extracted live. More complex timing, negation and follow-up summaries need held-out evaluation.

title: Text evaluation
notes: This is the new 16-case medication-name subset, not the full medical evaluation. Both models scored 14/16; both failed the two negation routes, and validation blocked each attempted write. Diverse fictional names were paired across otherwise identical Canadian English/French requests. 153 deterministic core tests passed. A small fixture set is not demographic or clinical validation.

title: Further evaluation
notes: Priorities are actual older-adult usability, bilingual acoustic tests, held-out complex visit transcripts and real-device latency/memory. No fine-tuning benefit or clinical accuracy claim is established here.
